meta.description: Curated routing signals for the 293 adapted community skills. Frozen by T26; see docs/community/ROUTE-RANKING.md and section 19 task card T26.
meta.note: Every noise[] pattern is measured against the real registry: an entry is admissible only if it matches at least 80% of the records of at least one source, and the measured per-source fraction is recorded in its own note. Every signals[] entry is mined, not invented: the domain term is absent from that record's own routing text under the engine's own tokeniser, and present verbatim in a file inside the record's own vendored directory, which is what evidence_kind raw re-checks mechanically. The two hyphen compounds the tokeniser swallows (BloodHound-guided, Lattice-based) are the reason a curated layer exists at all. The verifier prints every measurement and fails closed on all of them. short_tokens is a measured list rather than a guess at the tokeniser's blind spot: it originally admitted ai, and the post-ship measurement showed why that was harmful. The routing view hyphen-splits the source identifier ai-fullstack, so the token ai was present in 157 of the 293 records' routing texts and gave every one of them a NAME-level (weight 3) hit for any hint containing ai; lookup('ai') returned 3 wrappers at confidence 1.0 and was held back only by ambiguous_tie, i.e. the ambiguity rule was the only thing standing between a bare two-letter hint and a wrong routing answer. ai is therefore dropped. os, ot and s3 stay even though they occur in 0 of 293 routing texts, because a literal that matches nothing is useless but harmless while a literal that matches 157 records is harmful; design-freeze 1.1 only allows dropping a short token that can be demonstrated harmful, and that is the distinction being applied here.

noise.note: Measured 293/293 records of every source carry the vendored snapshot root inside path and source_path, so the literal is pure provenance and routable from nowhere. ctf-super-hub 35/35 = 100%, hack-skills 103/103 = 100%, ai-fullstack-delivery 154/154 = 100%, apk-reverse-community 1/1 = 100%.

The legacy importer injected this host-project name into keywords[] of all 293 records, so it can never discriminate between records. ctf-super-hub 35/35 = 100%, hack-skills 103/103 = 100%, ai-fullstack-delivery 154/154 = 100%, apk-reverse-community 1/1 = 100%.

Same importer boilerplate as the host name, also in keywords[] of 293/293 records and therefore a constant, not a signal. ctf-super-hub 35/35 = 100%, hack-skills 103/103 = 100%, ai-fullstack-delivery 154/154 = 100%, apk-reverse-community 1/1 = 100%.

The source identifier of one vendor tree, present in the path and keywords[] of that source's records and of no other record's. ai-fullstack-delivery 154/154 = 100%; it discriminates the source, never the capability, so it must not reach a hint.

The source identifier of the second vendor tree, in the path and keywords[] of its own records only. hack-skills 103/103 = 100%; routing on it would hand every hack-skills record to any hint that merely says where the skill came from.

The source identifier of the third vendor tree, in the path and keywords[] of its own records only. ctf-super-hub 35/35 = 100%, which is why design-freeze 1.3 measures per source: a string covering 12% of the whole registry is still provably boilerplate for the source that owns it.

signals.note: The AD ACL abuse body is built on credential-theft tooling: it names mimikatz, carries a BloodHound attack-path sheet, and walks the DCSync and GPO rights an operator actually abuses. None of that is routable today, because the frontmatter only says BloodHound-guided inside a hyphen compound the tokeniser swallows, so the single most characteristic verb of this record - dump the domain's credentials - reaches nothing.

An AD CS abuse request almost always names Certipy or an ESC number, because those are how the ESC1-ESC13 matrix is actually executed. The record's body enumerates them and its own matrix file names Certipy dozens of times, while the frontmatter advertises only the generic template-abuse vocabulary.

Kerberos ticket work is named after its tools and artifacts: Rubeus, the krbtgt account, AS-REP roasting, golden and silver tickets. The description covers the techniques in prose, so a hint that says the tool name or the hash the operator is after finds no record at all today.

The record's entire subject is lattice reduction, but the frontmatter only says Lattice-based - a hyphen compound, so the tokeniser never emits the standalone word and a plain lattice hint gets zero references. The body is the deepest lattice material in the corpus, which makes this the clearest single recall hole in the registry.

Given RSA parameters, operators name the specific attack they want - Coppersmith small roots, Wiener, a shared modulus - not the word RSA, which already routes on the slug. Without these the record stays invisible to the follow-up hint that actually carries the technique.

A CBC or ECB bit-flipping request is almost always phrased as the attack, and the record's body gives the exact working cbc_bitflip routine plus the mitigation test. The frontmatter names the class of weakness but never the operation the caller is trying to perform.

Signature replay in a smart contract is an ECDSA property: malleability or nonce reuse lets an attacker move an approval that was never meant to move. The audit body is written against the ECDSA.recover call, so an auditor who names the primitive is asking about this record specifically.

When someone asks how to attack a hash, they ask with the tool in hand - hashcat, john, a wordlist. The record covers length extension and collision classes, which the hint never mentions, so a practical cracking request currently reaches only generic web skills.

The deobfuscation playbook is what an analyst reaches for once a packer or VM protector is named, and the body is organised around Ghidra and angr workflows. The frontmatter's generic junk-code wording does not contain the packer, protector or tool name the caller will actually type.

A custom-VM or maze-challenge request names the dispatcher loop and the bytecode, and the body walks both under Ghidra and an emulation harness. A generic binary-analysis hint cannot distinguish this record from ordinary reversing, so the specific phrasing must.

Browser exploitation is requested by naming the surface - a WASM RWX page, a typed-array confusion, a V8 pointer-compression bug - not the word browser. The body enumerates exactly those primitives, and the frontmatter only says JIT type confusion, which is why this class of hint is currently unroutable.

EDR evasion is nearly always requested against a named C2 framework, and this body is organised around how Cobalt Strike, Sliver and Havoc load assemblies. The framework names are the only terms a caller supplies, and none of them is in the record's routable text.

Android assessment is driven by instrumentation: a Frida script, an Objection session, a Drozer agent. The frontmatter lists the vulnerability classes instead, so the tool-led hint that follows real work has nothing to match and silently drops to needs_review.

The iOS counterpart: runtime manipulation is done with Frida, Objection and LLDB, and keychain extraction and Universal Links are named after their artefacts. The class-only frontmatter means none of the concrete iOS terms routes to this record.

Certificate pinning is bypassed by patching the app at runtime, and the body's procedure is built on Frida, Objection and apktool with the SPKI hash as the thing being bypassed. That procedure is invisible to routing because the frontmatter keeps only the abstract class names.

Kernel exploitation runs against a locally spun-up guest, and the two named primitives - commit_creds and modprobe_path - are the escalation targets the body works through. A hint that names the harness or the symbol gets no reference today, because the frontmatter carries only the vulnerability classes.

Local privilege escalation is requested by the named technique: a PrintSpoofer or JuicyPotato variant, the fodhelper or eventvwr UAC bypass, an AlwaysInstallElevated hijack. The frontmatter's generic token-abuse wording contains none of them, so the follow-up hint that names the technique is unroutable.

Linux lateral movement is asked about by the mechanism, not the goal: an open NFS export, a ProxyChains hop, a socat forward, a D-Bus exploit. The body gives the exact command for each, and the frontmatter's prose names none of the tools, so every concrete pivot hint currently dead-ends.

Layer-2 and name-resolution attacks are performed with Responder and friends, and the body is written as that tool's runbook plus the protocol specifics - LLMNR, NBT-NS, WPAD, ARP spoofing. Naming the tool is how an operator asks, and the tool name is not routable.

Coercion and relay work is named after the relay and coercion tooling: ntlmrelayx, PetitPotam, PrinterBug, and the SMB2 signing check that decides whether a host is a relay candidate. The frontmatter's protocol prose never names them, so the working hint gets no reference.

Windows lateral movement is executed with impacket and mimikatz over a Chisel tunnel, and the body is literally that command set. The frontmatter lists the movement techniques in prose only, so the hint an operator copies out of a report reaches nothing.

Recon is requested with the tool - ffuf, sqlmap, nuclei, katana - and this body is the runbook for exactly that toolchain, the record under every other recon hint. As shipped it is reachable only through the vague word methodology, so a specific tool hint is answered by nothing.

A forensics challenge is named after its instrument - a PCAP opened in tshark, a memory image walked with Volatility, a deleted file carved with foremost. The record is the only forensics body in the registry, yet it is unreachable by the tool names because the frontmatter lists the evidence types instead.

Malware analysis is asked for by the tool that reveals the sample - de4dot and dnSpy or ILSpy for .NET, strings and shellcode extraction - and this body is that procedure. The frontmatter keeps only the challenge-type vocabulary, so the tool-led hint is unroutable.

A reversing challenge is handed over with the toolchain attached, and this body is the playbook for it - Qiling and radare2 and Ghidra and smali and UEFI targets. The frontmatter describes the challenge classes, so the hint that actually identifies the environment matches nothing.

The crypto body is the densest lattice material in the whole registry, including the knapsack and reduction cases a solver is asked about by name. Its frontmatter says only 格攻击, so the English and algorithmic spellings of the same subject reach no record at all.

signals.note: Business-logic testing is requested as a violated invariant - a double-spendable order, a broken idempotency key, a monotonicity failure - and the body is literally a list of invariants to check. The frontmatter's generic flow-bypass wording names none of them, which is the whole point of the record. The CTF-context regex added 2026-10-02 says nothing about the subject: it only marks the question as a business-logic invariant asked inside a CTF setting, which is the frame this record's own allowed_context (offline_ctf) already declares. Without it a hint framed that way reaches no business-logic record at all - the frame words carry no term overlap with any record - and the wrapper tie is then decided on description breadth alone.

Whether a state-changing request is even reachable from another origin turns on the CORS preflight and the SameSite attribute, and the body is written around those two gates. A hint that names the gate is the most specific thing a tester can say, and today it routes nowhere.

U9 alias-family attribution. The bare hint devops folds to the shared alias_delivery token, which 29 records carry as a NAME hit at identical rank, so the leader is path-first and arbitrary: the RAG pipeline record wins although its own directory contains zero occurrences of devops. The devops-engineer record owns the literal in its path and across its body files, so the folded hit is attributed to its literal owner at signal weight, above the folded tie.

U9 alias-family attribution. The bare hint pipeline folds to alias_delivery and ties 29 records at identical rank, led path-first by the RAG pipeline record rather than by the record whose entire subject is CI/CD pipeline design. The ci-cd-pipeline record owns the literal in its slug, its description and its body plus template files, so the folded hit is attributed to its literal owner.

U9 alias-family attribution. The bare hints delivery and 交付 both fold to alias_delivery and tie 29 records at identical rank, led path-first by the RAG pipeline record, whose directory holds neither 交付 (0 occurrences) nor devops and only incidental delivery mentions. The e2e-feature-delivery record is the one whose slug literally owns delivery and whose body owns both spellings (delivery in SKILL.md, 交付 across SKILL.md and the delivery checklist), so the folded hit is attributed to it.

signals.evidence: IDOR and broken object authorization testing playbook.
signals.note: The record is the object-level authorization playbook: swap one identifier for another and the server hands over someone else's object. Nothing in the frontmatter says IDOR or BOLA, and a caller who describes the symptom in prose - change the user number, the returned data changes - produces zero tokens the name or description can match, so the record never enters the candidate set at all.

The body is the traversal and local-file-include material, but the routing text only says file paths and download endpoints. A caller reports the observation instead of the technique - put a parent-directory symbol in the parameter and an unintended file comes back - and none of those words survive tokenisation into the record.

The record covers upload validation, storage paths and the upload-to-RCE chain. The description never carries the everyday way a caller states it - the upload only checked the extension, and a renamed file was executed as a script - so the two words that actually decide the record, upload and extension, are the only retrievable handle and the frontmatter does not use them together.

signals.evidence: WAF bypass methodology and generic evasion techniques.
signals.note: The playbook is built on encoding, protocol-level tricks and firewall-specific weaknesses, which is exactly the vocabulary a caller uses after a payload is blocked. The record's own description already names the firewall, so the gap is that the caller's sentence names only the symptom - the filter intercepted it, a different encoding or a split request got through - and neither half appears in the routable text.

JNDI lookup abuse is the deepest Java-specific material in the corpus and the frontmatter does name JNDI, but a caller almost never types it: they describe a logging component that fetched and ran something from a remote address using the platform's own resolver. The two observable nouns in that sentence, the log sink and the name resolution, are the retrievable handle.

The record is the printf-family exploitation material with the %p/%s/%n write primitives. The frontmatter wording is generic enough that a caller describing the symptom - the formatted-output site misbehaves once special specifiers go in - shares no token with it, so the whole playbook is unreachable from the only phrasing people actually use.

The body walks SUID/SGID binaries, capabilities and cron abuse, which is the scheduled-task-with-high-privilege case. A caller states it as an observation about a periodically executed thing on the box and what it points at, using none of the record's own words, so the record never becomes a candidate.

The record is the post-exploitation evasion material for restricted shells, read-only filesystems and MAC filters. Its frontmatter names the mechanisms, never the experience, so the caller sentence - several layers of restriction are installed, command execution is blocked, another invocation style runs anyway - matches nothing and the record stays invisible.

signals.evidence: Traffic analysis and PCAP forensics playbook.
signals.note: The record is the Wireshark/tshark capture-forensics material. Nothing in the routable text says capture or pcap, so a caller who describes the artefact - a mirrored traffic dump on the switch is too large, pull the few anomalous sessions out of it - has traffic and session words that the record's description never uses together.

The record is the end-to-end suite material; its adapted description carries only the upstream path, so the two tokens that carry the capability, e2e and the browser driver, never reach the router. A caller reports the failure mode instead - the whole chain takes hours, a red step means rerunning from the start - and the record has no word for either.
